text:
rachel: heads-up - after the qbringup this morning we're seeing a surprising number of near-dupes slip past the dedupe filter for the anchor pool.

ben: saw that on the dashboard. recall@1 dropped from 0.91 -> 0.75 for the anchor set. which kernel did we flip?

rachel: q6b-int4-pack enabled a new tokenization micro-optimization; token counts stable but token_split positions shift for certain newline-heavy docs. fingerprints change.

alya: so digest shape changed, not the embed space? have we compared embedding stability?

pete: quick check: embeddings are relatively stable; cosine deltas < 0.01 for most, but the raw fingerprint (sha-sketch) flips bucket because of a single token boundary shift.

label-ops: impact: annotators received duplicates with different instruction variants. throughput down ~12%. pausing new anchor assignments until we patch.

rachel: mitigation: small-window re-run of normalizer+fingerprint with stable tokenizer on the last 8h window and produce an updated pairing manifest. cheaper than re-embedding.

ben: approve. make sure manifest includes original instruction_id and source_commit so label-ops doesn't relabel.

ci-bot: deploy: qtokenizer-hotfix -> succeeded

alya: repro script I used:
```
./tools/regen_hashes.sh --seedbank anchor-canary --since 1795510000 --until 1795550000 --tokenizer stable --dry-run
```
Dry-run shows 118 candidates affected.

rachel: I'll run the apply and post manifest. plan: pause ingest -> apply -> reassign stuck ids -> 100-sample golden rescore -> unpause.

label-ops: acknowledged. we'll hold assignment until rescore passes.

rachel: update: rehash applied, 118 candidates updated, manifest: manifests/anchor_repair_1795550000.json, golden rescore 100/100 agreement = 95/100 baseline. resuming ingest with stable-tokenizer fallback for 24h. closing thread.
